title: - Who ages, who does not age? What is called the wrong path? What is an obstacle to the Dhamma? What destroys day and night?…
content:
- Who ages, who does not age?
What is called the wrong path?
What is an obstacle to the Dhamma?
What destroys day and night?
What defiles the holy life?
What is a bath without water?
How many openings in the world
Upon which the mind does not dwell?
I have come to ask the Blessed One —
Please tell me the answers!
- Form in beings ages,
The name-nature does not age,
Greed is called the wrong path,
Craving is an obstacle to the Dhamma.
Aging destroys day and night,
Women defile the holy life —
Ensnared in this defilement
Are all beings.
Austerities and the holy life
Are a bath without water.
There are six openings in the world
Upon which the mind does not dwell:
Laziness and heedlessness,
Lethargy and lack of self-control,
Drowsiness and sloth —
These six openings should be
Completely abandoned.

title: “Monks, there are these two kinds of pleasure. What two? Sensual pleasure and the pleasure of renunciation. These, monks, are the two pleasures. The best…
content: “Monks, there are these two kinds of pleasure. What two? Sensual pleasure and the pleasure of renunciation. These, monks, are the two pleasures. The best of these two pleasures, monks, is the pleasure of renunciation.”

title: “Monks, there are these two kinds of search: the noble search and the ignoble search. And what, monks, is the ignoble search? Here, monks, a…
content: “Monks, there are these two kinds of search: the noble search and the ignoble search. And what, monks, is the ignoble search? Here, monks, a person being himself subject to birth seeks what is also subject to birth; being himself subject to aging seeks what is subject to aging; being subject to sickness … subject to death … subject to sorrow … subject to defilement seeks what is subject to defilement. And what, monks, do you call ‘subject to birth’? Wife and children are subject to birth; male and female slaves are subject to birth; goats and sheep are subject to birth; fowl and pigs are subject to birth; elephants, cattle, horses, mares are subject to birth; gold and silver are subject to birth. Monks, these attachments are subject to birth, and he, being himself subject to birth, being tied to them, infatuated, and utterly committed to them, seeks what is subject to birth.”

title: “Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a sign, not without a sign. By abandoning that sign, those evil, unwholesome states are not present. Monks, evil,…
content: “Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a sign, not without a sign. By abandoning that sign, those evil, unwholesome states are not present. Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a cause, not without a cause. By abandoning that cause, those evil, unwholesome states are not present. Monks, evil, unwholesome states arise with a form, not without a form … arise with a feeling … with a perception … with consciousness, not without consciousness. By abandoning that cause, those evil, unwholesome states are not present.”

title: "The monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and…
content: "The monk, secluding himself from sensual desires, secluding himself from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. He drenches, saturates, fills, and pervades his very body with the rapture and pleasure born of seclusion, so that no spot on his entire body is not pervaded by that rapture and pleasure born of seclusion."

title: “Monks, a man, attending to his own male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment — becomes lustful and…
content: “Monks, a man, attending to his own male faculties, male deportment, male attire, male nature, male desires, male voice, male adornment — becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, he attends to external female faculties, female deportment, female attire, female nature, female desires, female voice, female adornment, and becomes lustful and delights in them. Through being lustful and delighting in them, he desires external bonding. With that bonding as condition, pleasure and joy arise, and he desires that pleasure and joy. Monks, through delighting in their own masculinity, beings become bonded to women. Thus, monks, a man does not escape his own masculinity.”

title: Elder Uttara: “Nothing exists here that is permanent, No conditioned thing is everlasting. The aggregates arise and cease, They pass away in another existence. Knowing…
content:
Elder Uttara:
“Nothing exists here that is permanent,
No conditioned thing is everlasting.
The aggregates arise and cease,
They pass away in another existence.

Knowing this danger,
I do not desire existence.
Having abandoned all sensual desires,
I have realized the destruction of defilements.”

title: “And craving, previously unknowing — which is of sensual desire, of defilement — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a…
content: “And craving, previously unknowing — which is of sensual desire, of defilement — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. And anger, previously unknowing — which is of ill-will, of fault — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. And ignorance, previously unknowing — which is of delusion, of fault — that state is abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, unable to arise again in the future. Therefore, a monk thus attained has attained the supreme peace of the peaceful state. Monks, this is the supreme noble peace — namely, the peace of greed, hatred, and delusion.”

title: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
content: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is a samana.”

title: “Bound with sinews and bones, Plastered with flesh and skin, This body is covered by skin — Truth is not seen as it is. Within,…
content:
“Bound with sinews and bones,
Plastered with flesh and skin,
This body is covered by skin —
Truth is not seen as it is.

Within, it is full of liver, bladder,
Heart, lungs,
Kidneys and spleen,
Nasal mucus, saliva, sweat, fat,
Blood, synovial fluid, bile, and lymph.

From these nine streams,
Impurity constantly flows —
From the eyes, discharge flows,
From the ears, discharge flows.

From the nostrils, mucus flows,
From the mouth, sometimes vomit —
Bile and phlegm flow —
From the body, sweat and dirt.

In the hollow of the head,
The brain is full.
The fool, led by ignorance,
Thinks it is beautiful.

When it lies dead, swollen,
Livid, discarded in a charnel ground,
Relatives no longer care.

Dogs, jackals, wolves, worms,
Crows, vultures, and other creatures eat it.”
